get.description:
Google redirects here after the shop owner authorises.

Logic:
  0. Verify the CSRF state against the state cookie (400 on mismatch)
  1. Exchange code for tokens
  2. Fetch userinfo (google_sub, email, name)
  3. Look up existing ShopOwner by google_sub first, then by email
  4a. Existing user with status='banned' → redirect with error=banned;
      status='suspended' (F5970) → neutral error=google_failed
  4b. Existing approved/pending user → log in, redirect with ?success=1
  4c. New user → create pre-signup ShopOwner (shop_id=NULL, status='pre_signup')
      → redirect with ?success=1&new_user=1
Bind a fresh state + PKCE verifier to the browser and redirect to Google.

`ShopListing.is_published` back to True for every ShopListing that
belongs to THIS case's items AND THIS case's shop — never other shops'
listings of the same (possibly duplicate-matched) item. This is the
resolution of the previously-documented Known Gap in
03-implementation.md §3.1.

Owner rejects the case with optional feedback -> automatic
reject-rework loop (Design §3.2/§10, BB-Entscheidung 14.7.):

  awaiting_owner_review -> rejected -> rework_in_progress

both in one call/transaction (Risk R4, 02-backend-architecture.md §8:
no intermediate commit between the two transitions), then re-dispatches
describe.item for EVERY catalog_case_item of the case with
owner_feedback=body.feedback (Design: feedback granularity is
case-level, not per-item — all items get reworked).

is_published stays False through reject/rework — only approve flips it
(F5980 addendum, Publish-Visibility-Gate). This endpoint intentionally
never writes ShopListing.is_published.

  4. Set shop.status = 'inactive'
  5. Set owner.status = 'inactive', anonymise email + clear google_sub
  6. Commit

DSGVO notification email is sent BEFORE email anonymisation (fire-and-forget).
